text: Using gpt2-small as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-3b as the strong student, we evaluated a learned noisy-channel model of weak-label errors refined by expectation-maximization with a single EM round (em_rounds: 1), averaged over 5 seeds. The weak supervisor reaches 0.49 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling is 0.66. Training the strong model through the noisy-channel correction yields a transfer accuracy of 0.55 (SE 0.01) and a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.38 with a standard error of 0.07, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.05. The PGR exceeds the baseline by more than two standard errors of the PGR estimate, so the method appears to recover a larger share of the weak-to-strong gap than the baseline under this setup. Caveats: the baseline is reported as a single number without its own standard error, only 5 seeds and one EM round were run, and the evaluation covers a single weak/strong model pair, so generalization to other pairs or more EM rounds is untested.
